items.problem: CS8803 'Top-level statements must precede namespace/type declarations' + CS1022 'end-of-file expected' + repeated CS0106 'modifier not valid' across Scenario1_LaunchFile.xaml.cs and Scenario2_LaunchUri.xaml.cs — caused by an extra/stray closing brace that prematurely closed the class+namespace so later members parsed as top-level statements.
items.evidence: session-log: Scenario1_LaunchFile.xaml.cs(206,9) CS8803; (208,9) CS0106 'public not valid'; (374,5)/(375,1) CS1022; build-events shows CS8803 x3 then recovery (18 total successful builds).
items.covered_clearly_at: N/A — this is a generic C# brace-balance editing typo, not a UWP→WinUI 3 migration API/pattern. No skill section could or should encode 'do not add a stray brace'.
items.why_no_skill_change: A capable model on re-run would balance braces correctly; it is an editing error, not a knowledge gap. Adding prose about brace balancing would only bloat the skill with anti-slip noise.
